newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan construction shares up on land auction.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan construction shares up on land auction.

text.p: Taiwan's construction shares rose in late Thursday trade on news that bidding prices at an auction of 10 state land parcels were much higher than the base prices, suggesting a property market recovery, brokers said.
With one hour left, Ruentex Construction had gained 20 cents or 1.1 percent to T$18.30 and Der Pao Construction was up 60 cents or 2.11 percent to T$29.00.
The entire construction sector was up 0.13 percent, bucking the trend of the main index which was down 0.12 percent on institutional selling.
Analysts were positive about the news. "The state land auction is seen as a good indication for the construction and real estate market," said Lin Long-hsien of United Securities.
Oliver Fang, international sales head at National Securities, said the results showed an expected recovery in the property sector was at hand.
"The better-than-expected auction results signal that the expected recovery may come earlier (than anticipated)," he said.
